title: Lesson 56 - That Came Across the Wrong Way

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: The client can open the file now, but they wrote, “Your last note came across as if the access problem were my fault.”

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: What exactly did you send?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: “Use the third link. Ignore the other two. Don't request access again.”

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: The instructions are clear, but three commands in a row can come across as blame.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I didn't mean it that way. I was trying to prevent another access request.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Your intention matters, but it doesn't erase the effect. Which sentence caused the most trouble?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: The sentence that says, “Don't request access again.” It sounds as if the client did something wrong.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Right. The strongest evidence is the client's own description, not a guess based on punctuation.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I can't conclude that they're angry. They might simply be explaining how the message sounded.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Good. What did you mean to say?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: What I meant was, “You shouldn't need to request access again. If the link still doesn't open, please let me know.”

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Better. Start by acknowledging the effect before explaining.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: “Thanks for flagging that. My last message came across more sharply than I intended.”

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Then identify the current file without making the client reconstruct your mistake.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: “To avoid confusion, the third link is the only current link. The first message had no attachment, and the second link did not include your access.”

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Good. Could you reset the interaction with one clear next step?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: “Could we reset and use the labeled version 3 link below? You shouldn't need any further permission.”

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Read the whole message aloud once.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I tried reading it as the recipient, and it sounds calmer. I'll send this one repair and stop creating new links.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Perfect. It accepts the effect, explains the evidence and leaves one usable action.

transfer.title: 客户留言（陌生英式女声）
transfer.instruction: 先听两遍，记录可打开的文件、产生责怪感的原句、语气限定、旧链接状态、无需重发的内容和回复期限。
transfer.speaker: Quinn
